title: Solving equations
intro: Find the mystery number. Keep the equation balanced: whatever you do to one side, do to the other.
description: Free KS3 Maths solving equations questions with answers: one-step and two-step equations, brackets, unknowns on both sides and writing your own equations. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9 (ages 9 to 14).

questions.hint: What number add 7 makes 12? Or: take 7 from both sides.
questions.explain: Take 7 from both sides: x = 12 − 7 = 5. Check: 5 + 7 = 12.

questions.hint: 4x means 4 × x. Divide both sides by 4.
questions.explain: Divide both sides by 4: x = 28 ÷ 4 = 7. Check: 4 × 7 = 28.

questions.hint: Add 9 to both sides.
questions.explain: Add 9 to both sides: x = 3 + 9 = 12. Check: 12 − 9 = 3.

questions.hint: Multiply both sides by 5.
questions.explain: Multiply both sides by 5: x = 6 × 5 = 30. Check: 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

questions.q: Which step gets rid of the "− 3" in 4x − 3 = 17?
questions.hint: Do the opposite of subtracting 3.
questions.explain: Adding 3 undoes subtracting 3: 4x − 3 + 3 = 17 + 3, so 4x = 20 and x = 5.

questions.hint: Take 9 from both sides.
The x can be on the right. Add 4 to both sides.
questions.explain: Add 4 to both sides: 14 = x, so x = 14. Check: 14 − 4 = 10.

questions.hint: First take 2 from both sides, then divide by 3.
First add 4 to both sides.
Take 9 from both sides. The answer can be negative.
Undo the ÷ 3 first by multiplying both sides by 3.
questions.explain: Multiply both sides by 3: x + 4 = 15. Then x = 11. Check: (11 + 4) ÷ 3 = 5.

questions.hint: Take 1 from both sides first, then divide by 2.
Add 2 to both sides first, then multiply by 4.
Add 3x to both sides so the x term is positive, then take 8 from both sides.
Take 3 from both sides. The answer does not have to be a whole number.
Take 2x from both sides so that x is only on one side.
Divide both sides by 3 first, or expand the bracket.
questions.explain: Divide by 3: x − 2 = 6, so x = 8. Check: 3 × (8 − 2) = 18.

questions.hint: Take 3x from both sides, then add 5.
Expand the bracket first: 6x + 2.
Take 2x from both sides.
Expand the bracket first: 5x − 5.
Take x from both sides, then take 10 from both sides. The answer can be negative.

questions.q: I think of a number and add 8. The answer is 20. What was my number?
questions.hint: Write it as n + 8 = 20.

questions.q: I think of a number, multiply it by 3 and then subtract 5. The answer is 16. What was my number?
questions.hint: Write it as 3n − 5 = 16, then solve.

questions.q: The angles of a triangle are x, 2x and 3x degrees. Angles in a triangle add up to 180°. What is x?
questions.explain: x + 2x + 3x = 6x, so 6x = 180 and x = 30. The angles are 30°, 60° and 90°.

questions.q: A rectangle is (x + 3) cm long and 4 cm wide. Its perimeter is 26 cm. Find x.
questions.hint: Perimeter = 2 × (length + width).
questions.explain: 2 × (x + 3 + 4) = 26 → x + 7 = 13 → x = 6. The rectangle is 9 cm by 4 cm, and 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26.

questions.q: Ben is 3 years older than Ada. Their ages add up to 25. How old is Ada?
questions.hint: Call Ada's age a. Then Ben's age is a + 3.

questions.q: Ella buys 5 cinema tickets that all cost the same. She pays £35 in total. How much is one ticket, in pounds?
questions.hint: Call the price of one ticket t. Then 5t = 35.

questions.q: A phone deal costs £15 up front, then £8 every month. So far Zara has paid £71 altogether. For how many months has she paid?
questions.hint: Write it as 15 + 8m = 71.

questions.q: Jo has 3 packs of football stickers and 5 loose stickers. Kai has 1 pack and 21 loose stickers. Every pack has the same number of stickers, and they have the same number of stickers in total. How many stickers are in a pack?
questions.hint: Call the number in a pack p. Then 3p + 5 = p + 21.
